_about: How a character learns what a reagent does, and who teaches formulae
beside herb-lore.json and smithing-lore.json, whose shape this mirrors, so one module
answers all three. Words, prices and times only: every number is the rules' own, so no
model ever authors one, and every one can be tuned in play without a code change.
Before this file (alchemy lane F, 2026-10-06) an alchemist's reagent answered to the
SMITH's rows (knowledge.craft_of): a blacksmith was camphor's teacher and a guildhall
its library. Lane A named the gap and left it for the bench lane with this file.
Prices are in copper (Core Rulebook Table 6-1); a lesson is priced as a healer's and a
smith's are, a skilled hireling's hour.

study._dc: 10 + 5 per rarity band, as herbs and metals (plan §13.2: 'the study DC, 10 + 5 per band').

teacher._works: Occupation ids (content/people/occupations.json) whose people know reagents: the new `alchemist` occupation (lane G, plan §14). 'apothecary' is NOT here: it is a match word of `healer`, which stays herbalism's (plan §14), so an apothecary teaches herbs. The words name the trade when no population record carries one.
teacher._teaches: Properties taught per lesson by attitude step (rules/attitude.py), the herb teacher's rows: below indifferent they refuse in words.

_formula_lesson: An alchemist teacher teaches any formula, the classics included (plan §10.4, 'fee, 1 h'); a companion who knows the spell teaches a spell formula free in 1 h a spell level. The fee is PROPOSED: the book's spellbook writing cost for the formula's spell level would charge nothing for a classic, so a teacher charges a lesson's fee per spell level, at least one.

library._common: What the world writes down about reagents: the benefits of common and uncommon ones. A rare reagent's secrets and every drawback stay unwritten, as for herbs and metals.

identify_potion._dc: DC 15 + the potion's spell level (plan §11.3; the CRB Potions page). The Perception table's '15 + caster level' was not taken; knowledge.POTION_IDENTIFY_DC says why.

_working_words: A working trait's line on a card (plan §5.5's table): what the trait does at the bench, in words. The numbers are the bench's rules (content/world-classes/alchemist.json), not this file's.

working_words.volatile: a roll failed by 5 or more flares in your face; a second volatile in the step adds 3 to the DC
working_words.stabilizer: calms one volatile input in the step it goes into
working_words.catalyst: never spent: set beside the work, it widens the step's window
working_words.apparatus: never spent: equipment that widens the step's window
working_words.solid: a solid: it calcines and sublimes, and dissolves
working_words.liquid: a liquid: it distills, filters and is a reaction's medium
working_words.combustible: it burns away rather than calcining
working_words.slow_to_dissolve: a narrower window when it is dissolved
working_words.light_sensitive: keep it sealed: it fades in the light
working_words.corrosive: eats a metal vessel; bottle it in glass or clay
working_words.toxic_to_handle: hurts the one who works it, unless a mask and gloves or a fume hood spare them
working_words.wild: copies one trait of another input in the step
working_words.drinkable: a vessel: what is bottled in it is drunk or poured on
working_words.shatters: a vessel: what is bottled in it is thrown and breaks
working_words.bursts: a vessel: what is bottled in it is thrown and bursts
working_words.struck: a vessel: what is bottled in it is a cloud, thrown or set off
working_words.stick: a vessel: what is bottled in it is a tool, struck or lit
working_words.fireproof: takes the heat of the bench
working_words.warded: holds what would eat an ordinary vessel
working_words.pure: the check is rolled twice, the better kept
